data.name: Efendi
data.gender_notes: Efendi is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A title of respect and honor given to a man of high status and education in Turkish and Ottoman culture. The name Efendi carries the meaning “Honorable sir” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Turkish. Parents who choose Efendi usually hope their child will grow to embody honorable sir and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A sign of respect and acknowledgement of the divine presence in a person.
data.etymology: Efendi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Honorable sir.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Efendi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: إفندي
in_arabic.meaning: صاحب منزل أو سيد محترم في المجتمع الإسلامي
in_arabic.long_meaning: إفندي هو لقب يطلق على الشخص الذي يتمتع بمكانة عالية في المجتمع الإسلامي، وغالبًا ما يُستخدم للإشارة إلى الشخص المتعلم أو الحاكم أو المسؤول. يعود أصل الكلمة إلى العربية وتعني صاحب المنزل أو السيد المحترم.

in_urdu.name: افندی
in_urdu.meaning: احترام کے ساتھ سيد یا گھر کا مالک
in_urdu.long_meaning: افندی ایک ایسا لقب ہے جو اسلامی معاشرے میں اعلیٰ مقام رکھنے والے شخص کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ یہ اکثر تعلیم یافتہ، حکمران یا عہدیدار شخص کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ اس لفظ کی اصل عربی ہے اور اس کا مطلب ہے گھر کا مالک یا قابل احترام سيد۔ جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں، افندی کو ایک فاضل اور علم کے حامل شخص کے طور پر سمجھا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: एफेंदी
in_hindi.meaning: एक सम्मानित व्यक्ति या घर का मालिक
in_hindi.long_meaning: एफेंदी एक ऐसा उपाधि है जो इस्लामी समाज में उच्च स्थान रखने वाले व्यक्ति के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। यह अक्सर शिक्षित, शासक या अधिकारी व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है। इसकी उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल से हुई है और इसका अर्थ है घर का मालिक या सम्मानित व्यक्ति। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, एफेंदी को एक विद्वान और ज्ञानी व्यक्ति के रूप में देखा जाता है।

in_pashto.name: افندی
in_pashto.meaning: د عزت لرونکی سړی یا د کور مالک
in_pashto.long_meaning: افندی داسې لقب دی چې په اسلامي ټولنه کې د لوړ مقام لرونکي کس لپاره کارول کیږي. دا اکثره د پوهان، واکمن یا چارواکي کس لپاره کارول کیږي. دا کلمه د عربي اصل څخه ده او د کور مالک یا د عزت لرونکي سړي معنی لري. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، افندی د يو محترم او دانشور شخص په توګه ګڼل کیږي.

in_english.name: Efendi
in_english.meaning: A respectful title for a learned or esteemed person
in_english.long_meaning: Efendi is a title of respect used in Islamic tradition for a learned, esteemed, or authoritative person. It originates from Arabic, meaning 'owner of the house' or 'respected lord.' Historically, it was used for scholars, rulers, or officials. The term signifies wisdom, knowledge, and social status. In modern times, it is used across Muslim cultures to denote a person of dignity and intellect.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Efendi" holds immense cultural significance in the Turkish and Ottoman societies. Historically, it was used as a title of respect and honor for individuals who possessed a high social status, often achieved through education, wealth or occupation. These individuals were well-versed in the Islamic and Ottoman traditions and culture, making them esteemed members of society. Today, while the use of the title is not as common as it once was, it is still used as a mark of recognition and respect towards an individual with great achievements or knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the title "Efendi" highlights the importance of education and knowledge as gateways to God. In Islamic teachings, knowledge is considered to be a sacred gift from God, and seeking it is a means of fulfilling one's religious and moral duties. The title "Efendi" signifies an individual who has dedicated themselves to this pursuit of knowledge, and in doing so, has drawn closer to God and His teachings. Thus, the use of this title is a reminder of the deep spiritual connection between learning, spiritual growth, and the pursuit of a righteous and virtuous life in accordance with Islamic values.
